mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 6 months signals an accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 6 months, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0% and rises by more than 0.1 percentage points over 3 months, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases corporate borrowing costs, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and rising (3-month change > 0.1pp), or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in unemployment rate and increases in non-farm payrolls signal a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods where UNRATE declines and PAYEMS increases simultaneously, or the Rank IC for the interaction term over the last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During housing market expansion (HOUST > 1600 thousand units) with rising consumer spending (RSAFS increasing), strong demand for goods and services supports corporate revenue growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods where HOUST > 1600 and RSAFS is rising (3-month change > 0.5%), or the Rank IC for the joint condition over the last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production falls below 110 and declines by more than 0.5% over 3 months, it signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate output and profit growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where INDPRO < 110 and declining (3-month change < -0.5%), or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation exceeds 3.0% and accelerates by more than 0.5 percentage points over 12 months, it signals persistent high inflation that triggers central bank tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods where CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and accelerating (12-month change > 0.5%), or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real consumer spending (RSAFS) over the prior 6 months signals robust household demand that supports corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods where RSAFS has increased over the prior 6 months, or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: During manufacturing expansion (INDPRO > 115 and rising), strong industrial output supports corporate production capacity and profit growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods where INDPRO > 115 and rising (3-month change > 0.5%), or the Rank IC over the last 5 years is below 0.05.
